editorial:
Ever felt like the world treats you like a side character while everyone else gets to be the star? You will totally relate to the main character in this wild ride. She starts as a tired restaurant worker who just can't catch a break, but everything changes when she gets sucked into a magical TV. Suddenly, she is a student at a school where they teach you how to be the perfect movie villain. It is a bright, colorful, and loud movie that feels like a giant party on screen. You get to see her go from being a shy pushover to a confident bad girl, and the comedy hits just right because it pokes fun at all those over-the-top soap opera tropes we all love to hate.

The acting is top-notch, especially the teachers at the academy who chew up every scene with huge energy. The pacing is quick, so you will not find yourself checking your phone. While some of the plot twists are a bit predictable, the heart of the story makes up for it. You should definitely watch this if you need a laugh or a little bit of revenge fantasy. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the crazy costumes. If you are a big fan of the director, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for those repeat viewings.
endingExplained: In the end, she realizes that being a villain is not about being mean, but about having power over your own life. She uses her new skills to face her real-world bullies and stands up for herself. The big twist is that the TV was a test to see if she had the guts to lead. She chooses to return home, but she keeps her confidence and becomes her own hero instead of a villain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky comedies and underdog stories.
